_meta.description: Prose content for the main About page. All numbers reference stored artifacts via validation_results.json or scoring_policy.json. Status draft = needs owner review before publishing.

goal.text: I built this site to be the one place you need when watching your daily game. Want to check out that funky lefty coming out of the pen, or see why your favorite star is in a slump? The site combines Baseball Savant’s easy visual comparisons with FanGraphs’ detailed stats and models, so you can see what’s driving a player’s success without three tabs open.

about_me.text: I’m a third-year economics student at the University of Toronto, and I’ve always loved watching baseball and studying sabermetrics. I haven’t played baseball at a high level, but I’m a competitive Muay Thai fighter and coach. In my spare time, I build any model or graph I find myself wondering about while watching the game. I also built Luck+, a model of MLB team luck, and this dashboard grew out of that work.

model_blurbs.stuff_plus: Grades the physical shape of a pitch: velocity, movement, spin, and release geometry, independent of where it was thrown or the count.
model_blurbs.location_plus: Grades where a pitch was thrown relative to the zone and the count, independent of what the pitch itself looks like.
model_blurbs.tunneling_plus: Grades how indistinguishable a pitcher's pitches look from each other, from release all the way to the plate.
model_blurbs.deception_plus: Grades release mechanics (arm slot, extension, release point) as predictors of outcomes, independent of pitch shape.

items: All four models explain a small share of per-pitch variance (R² 0.0002–0.007): a real signal, but a thin slice of any single pitch.
Stuff+'s out-of-sample stability (r=0.558) trails its in-sample fit (r=0.907), suggesting some memorization of pitcher-season patterns.
Location+ measures where a pitch ended up, not intent: a missed spot that lands well still scores as good command.
Deception+ can still partly track pitcher identity through arm slot and extension (ICC 0.90–0.99), even after removing the most identity-prone features.
Small samples are noisy. Only Stuff+ currently applies shrinkage, so scores under ~300 pitches should be read with caution.
All four models include season as a feature and need an annual retrain once a new season accumulates enough data.
Pitcher archetype profiles: group by arsenal shape and sequencing style rather than a single ranked score.
Run the pitcher-holdout identifiability audit (done for Stuff+ and Deception+) on Location+ as well.
Video-derived biomechanics for Deception+: pose tracking from broadcast video to capture timing and concealment Statcast doesn't record.
A combined view showing all four scores for one pitcher side-by-side, with disagreement between them highlighted.
Finish integrating the 3D tunneling viewer prototype into the site.
